statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-4360: TarFile.extract() did not pass the extraction filter on when extracting a hard link's target, so the filter's uid/gid and permission changes were not applied to it. Upstream fixed it in https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/151987 (3.12 commit https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/0367912be336348b30572f8029cec4a282782d92), first released in CPython 3.12.14; see https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-4360. Checked Lib/tarfile.py for extract() passing filter_function to _extract_one() in the python-3.12 package of every build published in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository, 3.12.12-r0 to 3.12.16-r4, x86_64 and aarch64; both architectures agree. Builds before 3.12.14-r1 lack the fix; 3.12.14-r1 and every later build have it. The range ends at 3.12.14-r1.

CVE-2026-4360: TarFile.extract() in the tarfile module did not pass its filter on when extracting a hard link, so a program that extracts an untrusted tar archive with filter='data' could still write files with an unexpected uid or gid. Upstream fixed it in https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/151987 (3.13 commit https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/eee3ddf0ca10283cc7fea724aae9cd8665f8d15e), first released in CPython 3.13.15; see the advisory https://mail.python.org/archives/list/security-announce@python.org/thread/TWZW2PC2AZOV6FENIHFSRC63OM7MBGSB/ and https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-4360. Each build carries the CPython release named by its version, as the version string in libpython3.13 shows. We read Lib/tarfile.py in every published build of the DHI Alpine 3.23 python-3.13 package (3.13.12-r0 to 3.13.18-r4, x86_64 and aarch64): the builds before 3.13.15-r0 carry CPython 3.13.14 or older and their extract() calls _extract_one() without the filter, while every build from 3.13.15-r0 on carries 3.13.15 or later and passes it. The range ends at 3.13.15-r0, the first build with the fix.
